findings.failure_path: The shortcut now requires re-entry only for shared deterministic gates or cross-repo contract/status/version/release semantics. The original rule, retained in stage-classify-and-route.md:15, also covers shared semantics within one repository and compatibility changes. A narrow fix to a shared status or compatibility contract can therefore route directly to its implementation owner without reaching shared-gate classification. Because ownership appears settled, the optional classification-reference load does not repair this narrowing.
findings.smallest_fix: Restore the full shared/cross-repo contract/status/version/release/compatibility predicate in the entry's shortcut exception.

findings.failure_path: The entry now loads implementation-completeness-and-minimality.md only for behavior-changing delivery and only before mapping. The old mandatory read before implementation and again before completion—including work claiming a refactor/mechanical exemption—survives only in stage-classify-and-route.md:123. A refactor with settled class and ownership can skip that optional reference; neither mandatory implementation-stage reference restores this directive. The exemption can consequently be claimed without reaching its classification rule.
findings.smallest_fix: Keep the pre-implementation and pre-completion load instruction, including claimed mechanical/refactor exemptions, in the entry or the mandatory implementation-stage references.

findings.failure_path: Changing software-architecture from leaf to entry advertises a direct route for backend design, while the following redirect sends only multi-stage architecture delivery through product-rd-workflow. A standalone backend-design request can follow this catalog directly to architecture, bypassing the product workflow that the requester explicitly requires as its entry.
findings.smallest_fix: Retain the leaf designation and state that backend designs enter product-rd-workflow before loading software-architecture.
